title: SRE incident communications runbook — templates & war-room checklist
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft runbook for incident communications focused on three deliverables: status page templates, external (customer) comms, and an internal war-room checklist. Goal: provide clear, safe, timely information while minimizing customer confusion and SRE cognitive load during incidents.

When to use:
- Any SEV2/SEV1 incident that impacts customer functionality, performance, or availability (hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Any cross-team outage where multiple orgs are pulled into the war-room.

Ownership model (quick reference):
- Comms lead: on-call SRE (primary) or SRE lead (if escalated) — responsible for external messages and status page updates.
- War-room facilitator: on-call SRE or triage lead — runs checklist and coordinates action items.
- Engineering owner(s): area owners (serving runtime, platform, infra) — responsible for remediation steps and root cause analysis.
- Customer Success / Account Ops: notified when customers are impacted for high-touch outreach.

Severity mapping (recommended):
- SEV1: total or near-total outage for a significant portion of customers, immediate attention, continuous updates.
- SEV2: degraded functionality or elevated error rates/latency with clear customer impact, frequent updates.
- SEV3: partial/non-critical degradation, scheduled updates or ad-hoc as needed.

Status page templates (short, safe, timestamped)
-- Template fields to always include:
  - Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}
  - Short title: 1-line summary
  - Status: INVESTIGATING | IDENTIFIED | MITIGATING | RECOVERED | POSTMORTEM
  - Affected services: list (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private / Console / Observability)
  - Customer impact: short plain-language sentence
  - Next update ETA: relative or absolute time (e.g., ~15 minutes)
  - Link to interim incident doc (war-room doc or internal incident channel)

Template: Investigating
  Title: API error spike impacting request routing — INVESTIGATING ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
  Body: We are aware of increased 5xx errors and delayed responses for the Redwood API. Our engineering team is investigating the root cause. Impacted customers may see intermittent failures or timeouts. We will provide an update by {{NEXT_UPDATE}}.

Template: Identified
  Title: Root cause identified — serving runtime overload ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
  Body: We have identified an issue in the serving runtime that causes request queues to grow under certain request patterns, leading to increased errors and latency. Engineering is implementing mitigations now. Affected services: Hosted API and Dedicated. Next update by {{NEXT_UPDATE}}.

Template: Mitigating
  Title: Mitigation in progress — scaling and routing changes being applied ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
  Body: We are applying routing fallback and temporary capacity scaling. Early signs indicate reduced errors for some traffic. We will confirm recovery status in the next update.

Template: Resolved
  Title: Incident resolved — full service restored ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
  Body: The issue has been resolved and services are operating normally. Root cause, timeline, and customer impact summary will be published in the postmortem. If you continue to experience issues, please contact support.

Customer communication templates (short-first, then detailed follow-up)
Principles:
- Lead with what customers care about: impact and how it affects them (not implementation details).
- Be honest about unknowns, promise next update windows, then meet them.
- Use plain language, avoid internal jargon (e.g., "KV cache warmup") in customer-facing messages.

Short customer notification (initial):
  Subject: Redwood API: Service disruption — we’re investigating ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
  Body: Hello — we’re currently investigating an issue affecting the Redwood API which may cause intermittent failures or increased latency for some requests. Our team is actively working to restore normal operation and we will share an update by {{NEXT_UPDATE}}. We apologize for the disruption.

Detailed customer update (interim):
  Subject: Update on {{INCIDENT_ID}} — mitigation underway
  Body: Hello — we identified the cause as high request queueing in the serving runtime under specific traffic patterns. We have applied routing fallbacks and temporary capacity increases for affected clusters. Customers using Hosted API should see reduced errors; Dedicated customers with pinned capacity may require manual failover — your CSM has been notified. We estimate full recovery in the next {{EST_RECOVERY_WINDOW}}.

Post-incident customer summary (follow-up):
  Subject: Post-incident summary — {{INCIDENT_ID}} (service restored)
  Body: Brief timeline (UTC):
  - {{T0}} Incident started — increased 5xx and latency observed
  - {{T1}} Root cause identified — serving runtime queueing under load
  - {{T2}} Mitigations applied — routing fallback and scaling
  - {{T3}} Service restored
  Impact summary: percentage of requests affected, avg duration of errors, affected product surfaces.
  Follow-up actions: planned mitigations, config changes, and expected ETA for permanent fix.
  Link to postmortem: {{POSTMORTEM_LINK}}

Internal war-room checklist (rapid execution flow)
Phase 0 — Triage (first 10 minutes)
  - Create incident channel: #sre-incident-{{INCIDENT_ID}} and invite: on-call SRE, owning team, SRE lead, SRE tooling, product/CS if customer-facing.
  - Assign roles: Comms lead, War-room facilitator, Triage owner, Customer liaison.
  - Set incident doc: /tmp/incident-{{INCIDENT_ID}} or Confluence incident draft and paste initial notes.
  - Post initial status page note: "INVESTIGATING" with T+15 update promise.

Phase 1 — Stabilize (10–60 minutes)
  - Collate logs/metrics: error rates, latency p95/p99, tail latencies, resource metrics (CPU/GPU queues), traffic distribution.
  - Short-term mitigations: circuit-breaker, routing fallback, temp scale up, cache flush — owner must document action and rollback steps.
  - Customer impact assessment: which tiers/regions/customers are affected? Tag customers and notify CSM if required.
  - Update status page: move to IDENTIFIED or MITIGATING with ETA for next update.

Phase 2 — Recover (60–240 minutes)
  - Validate recovery across regions and client SDKs. Run synthetic checks for critical paths.
  - If recovered, update status page to RECOVERED and start collecting timeline for postmortem.
  - If not recovered, escalate to SRE lead/Director and consider cross-region failover or feature gates.

Phase 3 — Post-incident (after service restored)
  - Draft postmortem outline within 48 hours (owner: incident lead).
  - Customer follow-up: send post-incident summary to affected customers within 72 hours (or earlier for major outages).
  - Action items: assign owners, due dates, and link to roadmap/plans for permanent fixes.

Communication cadence guidance:
- SEV1: updates every 15 minutes for first hour, then every 30 minutes until stable.
- SEV2: updates every 30 minutes for first 2 hours, then hourly.
- SEV3: ad-hoc updates or every 4–6 hours as needed.
Always set and meet the NEXT_UPDATE timestamp in every communication. Missing promised windows degrades trust more than a conservative cadence.

Slack posting quick-links & checklist
- Post in #sre-incident-{{INCIDENT_ID}} first. Use the status page snippet and short customer-facing blurb.
- Emoji status prefixes: :rotating_light: INVESTIGATING, :mag_right: IDENTIFIED, :hammer_and_wrench: MITIGATING, :white_check_mark: RESOLVED
- Pin links: incident doc, status page, primary dashboards, and PRs/rollbacks currently running.

Escalation matrix (who to call if blocked):
  - On-call SRE -> SRE lead -> Director SRE -> CTO (if customer-impacting > 2 hours and high revenue impact)
  - For legal/compliance/regulatory involvement (Private deployments): notify Security & Legal immediately.

Safe language examples (to avoid):
- Avoid: "root cause is a race condition in the KV allocator" (internal jargon)
- Prefer: "a concurrency issue in an internal request queue caused requests to back up under a specific pattern"

Incident checklist: quick copy-paste for the channel
  :rotating_light: INCIDENT {{INCIDENT_ID}} — short title
  Status: INVESTIGATING
  Impact: short sentence about who is affected
  Comms lead: @username | War-room facilitator: @username
  Next update: {{NEXT_UPDATE}}
  Links: incident doc | status page | dashboards

Postmortem & customer follow-ups
- Immediately collect timeline, evidence (logs, traces), and config changes applied during the incident.
- Postmortem should include: summary, impact, timeline, root cause, mitigations applied, action items (owner + due date), and follow-up comms plan.
- Tag the postmortem with impacted product areas and link the status page and incident channel.

Appendix: pre-written snippets (copy into status page or emails)
- Holding statement for long-running investigations: "We are still actively investigating and have engineers working around the clock. We know this is disruptive and will provide an update by {{NEXT_UPDATE}}. Thank you for your patience."
- When rolling back a release: "We are rolling back the recent deploy to restore baseline behavior. This may cause temporary fluctuations; we will update when the rollback completes."
- When a customer requests SLA credit info: "We will include an impact assessment in the postmortem with data needed to process SLA requests. Please open a ticket with your account team and reference {{INCIDENT_ID}}."

Open questions / TODOs for this draft:
- Define exact SLAs for update cadence per customer tier (PLG vs enterprise).
- Authorize standard templates for legal-sensitive language for Private deployments.
- Integrate automation to push status page updates from the incident doc to avoid manual copy errors.

Notes to self (internal):
- Keep language short and actionable; prefer bullet points over long paragraphs.
- Experiment with a single-button status page publish from the incident doc.
- Collect feedback from CS on clarity of customer messages after next SRE postmortem.

Document history:
- v0.1 (2025-11-07) initial draft
- v0.2 (2026-02-20) incorporated SRE lead feedback on escalation and cadence

End of runbook draft.
